precepts.text: The same power made Aaron's rod bud, bloom blossoms, and yield almonds overnight.
precepts.point: Gideon asks the fleece signs: dew on the fleece only with dry earth beside, and then the reverse, dew on all the ground with the fleece dry. The Lord commands the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleases; God can do whatever he wants, infinite power.

note.label: Judges 6: The Call of Gideon: Why Is All This Befallen Us

precepts.why:
The Lord commanded the dew, the condensation that falls through the night, to land exactly where he pleased: on the fleece only with the earth dry beside it, and then dry on the fleece with dew on all the ground. God can do whatever he wants; infinite power.

The same power made Aaron's rod bud overnight: “on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds.” A dead rod bore fruit in a night, just as a bowl full of water was wrung out of a fleece on dry ground.

points: Every tribe took a rod, a stick or staff, according to the house of their fathers, twelve rods, and the prince of every tribe wrote his name upon his rod; Aaron's name was written upon the rod of Levi.
The rods were laid up in the tabernacle of the congregation before the testimony, the ark of the covenant, where the Lord met with them; the man's rod whom the Lord chose would blossom and grow.
By this the Most High would make the murmurings of the children of Israel to cease from him, showing them that he was dealing with Moses and Aaron and them alone.
Every prince gave Moses a rod, one for each according to their fathers' houses, twelve rods, and the rod of Aaron was among them, and Moses laid them up before the Lord in the tabernacle of witness.
On the morrow, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds; and every man took back his own rod.

The Lord commanded Aaron's rod to be brought again before the testimony, to be kept for a token against the rebels, to take away their murmurings from the Lord, that they die not; so he would not have to put them to death again for murmuring.
And Moses did as the Lord commanded him.
The children of Israel cried, behold, we die, we perish, we all perish: whosoever cometh any thing near unto the tabernacle of the Lord shall die.
You had to be of Levi to go near the tabernacle; that had to be your office. The next chapter explains who was to minister there.
